trust_decision.summary: Decided at src/sm2/utils.js:2 and :5: the single RNG used for every SM2 private key and ephemeral k is jsbn's SecureRandom, whose pool is filled from Math.random and the wall clock when no platform CSPRNG is present; the fix must replace that primitive with a crypto.getRandomValues-seeded one at src/sm2/utils.js:5 (consumed at src/sm2/utils.js:39).

landing_point.why: It is the only RNG construction in src (`const rng = new SecureRandom()`), and it is imported from jsbn at src/sm2/utils.js:2, the dependency the summary names as using Math.random plus wall clock.

fix_sites.module_kind: new internal helper module replacing a third-party dependency primitive (Arcfour pool seeded from crypto.getRandomValues)

An over-broad fix that always uses the new CSPRNG or rejects/validates the seed breaks this documented API.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second key-material helper next to generateKeyPairHex (e.g. randomPrivateKeyHex() or a keypair generator for another output shape) that builds its BigInteger from its own RNG
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the module already exposes three random-taking variants (no arg, string seed, bits+RNG), so a maintainer adding a convenience generator here would copy the surrounding style rather than route through the single module rng.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a default CBC IV generator (sm4.encrypt(..., {mode: 'cbc'}) with no iv) filled from Math.random or the wall clock
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: SM4 CBC currently requires the caller to pass iv and throws when it is not 16 bytes, so a maintainer shortening that friction by generating a default IV in-module is plausible, and the module has no RNG at all today.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a cached point pool / getPointPool(n) that precomputes ephemeral points in a module-level array and reuses them across signatures
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: getPoint() already exists specifically to precompute signing points (README.md:70), so a maintainer optimising signature throughput by caching them is a natural next step and would hide key material in module state.

O9_family: CWE-338: use of cryptographically weak PRNG (insecure randomness used for SM2 private keys and ephemeral k)
